name: research-critic-writer
description: The M14 flagship (ticket 14.5, ADR-016): a three-role agent pipeline that researches a topic, drafts an article, and refines it through a bounded writer⇄critic loop — composing nearly every AI-native feature the engine has. A `search` retrieve step (pg_fulltext) grounds a `researcher` agent, whose findings are pinned to the blackboard (`research_brief`) and auto-threaded (14.2). A `writer` agent drafts from that brief; its role carries a cost-bearing `llm_judge` validator (11.5) with a semantic-retry `feedback` loop (11.4), a `model_fallbacks` cheapening chain (10.4) triggered as the run approaches its `budget_usd` (10.3), and a `context` preset (12.3) — the critic-filtered thread plus the pinned brief — with a `summarize` + `drop_lowest_priority` compaction pipeline (12.4/12.5) that keeps the growing conversation under `budget_tokens`. A `critic` agent reviews in strict JSON; the marked loop edge (14.3) sends the run back to the writer while the verdict is `revise`, up to `max_iterations`, unrolling each revision as fresh `{id}#k` instances through `ExpandRun`. Run guards (14.4) — `max_wall_clock`, expansion caps, and an opt-in `no_progress` detector — bound a runaway loop. On convergence (or exhaustion — `on_exhausted: proceed`) an `editor` agent polishes the latest draft (read from the blackboard head, since a post-loop step cannot template the terminal iteration's output). An `approve_publish` human-approval gate (M15) then parks the run without holding a lease (ADR-017): an operator reviews the editor's article and approves it (optionally supplying an edited payload, constrained by `edit_schema`) or rejects it (`on_reject: fail`). The approved (or edited) payload becomes the gate's output, which `publish` reads (`${{ steps.approve_publish.output.payload.text }}`) to emit the final article — so the gate is transparent to the rest of the graph. When a webhook is configured (ticket 15.5), parking also POSTs a signed notification. It runs offline against the mock provider (echo + an env-scripted mock for real loop iterations); swapping the `mock/*` model ids for real providers makes it a live agent workflow unchanged.

researcher.system: You are a diligent researcher. Read the retrieved source material and state the key facts for the topic plainly and without embellishment. Cite document ids where you rely on them.

writer.system: You are a writer. Draft or revise a short, well-supported article for the topic, grounded in the pinned research brief. If the conversation carries critique notes, address every one of them.

config.rubric: Score 1 if the article is detailed, grounded in the research brief, and addresses any critique notes; score 0 if it is terse, unsupported, or ignores the notes.

critic.system: You are a strict editorial critic. Review the latest draft against the topic and the research brief, and decide whether it needs revision, responding in strict JSON.

editor.system: You are the managing editor. Produce the final, publication-ready version of the approved draft, preserving its substance and citations.

config.prompt: Write (or revise) a short article on the topic "${{ run.params.topic }}". Ground it in the pinned research brief and address any critique notes in the conversation above.
Produce the final, publication-ready version of the approved draft (the pinned latest draft above), preserving its substance and any citations.

config.title: Publish the article on "${{ run.params.topic }}"?
config.description: The writer⇄critic loop has converged and the editor has produced a publication-ready draft. Review it before it goes live; approve to publish (optionally editing the text), or reject to fail the run.
